newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Acacia's Helix buy seen as expensive.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Acacia's Helix buy seen as expensive.

text.p: Major gold producer Acacia Resources Ltd surprised the market on Friday with a A$38 million play for Gawler Craton explorer Helix Resources NL, suffering a quick share price dip on concern it had paid too much.
Acacia dismissed speculation about a pending takeover bid, describing its 17.4 percent holding as a strategic stake.

"We have no intention at this stage of doing anything like that (launching a takeover bid)," managing director Michael Folie told Reuters, saying Acacia had built up its stake progressively at an average A$4.20 a share.
"We are sitting around this sort of number (17.4 percent) because we want to continue to assess the prospectivity of (Helix's Tunkillia prospect)," he said.
"If it gets bigger and larger we can then assess what the value of our holding is," he said.
The Gawler Craton region in South Australia is regarded as highly prospective for gold and has been the subject of intense exploration and share market scrutiny in recent months.
Helix's share price has surged from around 40 cents last October to reach a record A$4.98 in trading on Friday, buoyed by promising results at Tunkillia, near Lake Everard.
Following Friday's announcement, Acacia's price dipped 20 cents to A$2.19 before closing on Friday at A$2.24, down 15 cents on the day.

"The perception amongst some investors is that Acacia has paid top dollar for Helix and this has created some uncertainty about the outlook for the company," said Martin Angel, a dealer at Perth broker Eyres Reed.
An analyst who did not want to be named said he saw Helix currently as overvalued or at least fully priced, with a market capitalisation over that of producers with proven reserves.
Another said Acacia's move on Helix, to be funded by debt, was very surprising, both in terms of price and strategy, saying the junior was "pure blue-sky exploration stuff at this stage".
However, another analyst said he believed Acacia had a long term view on the purchase.
"If this thing comes up with the mega-million ounces, then they are obviously hoping it is going to be cheap," he said, adding he considered a takeover bid unlikely at this stage.
"It's a comfortable little stake, I think they will basically wait and see," he said.

Folie, who said the Craton was emerging as a region capable of containing world class gold deposits, defended the company's move, saying a very large ore body was possible at Tunkillia and that Helix's position was better than other Gawler stocks.

"It is not just pure exploration ... it has moved a bit beyond that and that of course means things tend to be a little bit more expensive," he said, adding he did not consider the stock overpriced given its results and potential.

Attention on the Gawler Craton stocks is expected to intensify in the coming weeks as work resumes after the Christmas lull and intense heat in the remote outback region which has forced much drilling to be done at night.

Analysts contacted by Reuters nominated Minotaur Gold NL, Pima Mining NL, Equinox Resources NL, Merritt Mining NL, and Grenfell Resources NL as stocks to watch with continuing interest expected from major gold producers, from Australia and offshore, in gaining access to the region.
"I would imagine there are other majors looking at the area," one analyst said.
"I just hope they are not all looking at Helix because there are better stories, I think, going to come out in the next six months," he said.
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
